{{Short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:JFB-Profile4.jpg|thumb|A recent picture of Jeffrey Brock]]
'''Jeffrey Farlowe Brock''' (born June 14, 1970, in [[Bronxville, New York]]) is an American mathematician, working in low-dimensional [[geometry]] and [[topology]]. He is known for his contributions to the understanding of [[hyperbolic 3-manifold]]s and the geometry of [[Teichmüller space]]s.

Since July 2018, Brock has been a professor of mathematics at [[Yale University]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://news.yale.edu/2018/03/28/yale-appoints-mathematician-jeff-brock-first-fas-dean-science|title=Yale appoints mathematician Jeff Brock as first FAS dean of science|date=2018-03-28|work=YaleNews|access-date=2018-03-28|language=en}}</ref> and in January 2019 he became the first FAS (Faculty of Arts and Sciences) dean of science at Yale.<ref name=":1" /> In July 2019, he was additionally appointed Dean of the [[Yale School of Engineering & Applied Science]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://news.yale.edu/2019/07/31/jeffrey-brock-named-dean-yale-school-engineering-and-applied-science|title=Jeffrey Brock named dean of Yale School of Engineering and Applied Science|access-date=2021-08-03}}</ref>

Before joining [[Yale University|Yale]], he was a professor at [[Brown University]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.brown.edu/~brock/|title=Jeffrey F. Brock - Home|website=www.math.brown.edu|access-date=2018-03-19|archive-date=2018-03-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180321212125/https://www.math.brown.edu/~brock/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and also founding director of the Data Science Initiative<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brown.edu/initiatives/data-science/about/people/people-executive-committee|title=People: Executive Committee {{!}} Data Science Initiative|website=www.brown.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-03-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180908202217/https://www.brown.edu/initiatives/data-science/about/people/people-executive-committee|archive-date=2018-09-08|url-status=dead}}</ref> at Brown University.

== Biography ==
Brock obtained a BA (with distinction in [[Mathematics]]) from [[Yale University]] in 1992. He completed a Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1997, under the supervision of [[Curtis T. McMullen]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=32226|title=Jeffrey Brock – The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2018-03-19}}</ref>

Brock then held positions as (NSF-funded) Szego Assistant Professor <ref name=":0" /> at [[Stanford University]] (1997–2000), assistant professor <ref name=":0" /> at the [[University of Chicago]] (2000–2003), and Donald D. Harrington Faculty Fellow <ref name=":0" /> at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] (2003–2004). He became associate professor with tenure at [[Brown University]] in 2004, and a full professor in 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.brown.edu/people.html|title=People of the Math Department|last=department|first=PAUR Web|website=www.math.brown.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-03-19|archive-date=2018-04-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180420010515/https://www.math.brown.edu/people.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was chair of the Mathematics Department from 2013 to 2017.

Brock has been associate director of [[ICERM]] since 2013. Previously, he had been deputy director between 2010 and 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://icerm.brown.edu/people/|title=ICERM|website=icerm.brown.edu|access-date=2018-03-19}}</ref>

Since July 2018, Brock has been a professor of mathematics at [[Yale University]],<ref name=":1" /> and in January 2019 he became the first FAS (Faculty of Arts and Sciences) dean of science at Yale.<ref name=":1" /> In July 2019, he was additionally appointed Dean of the [[Yale School of Engineering & Applied Science]].<ref name=":2" />

Brock is also an accomplished [[jazz]] musician. He was the founding bassist of the Vijay Iyer Trio, led by the acclaimed jazz pianist [[Vijay Iyer]].

He is married and has three children.

== Research ==
Jeffrey Brock's research focuses on [[low-dimensional topology]] and geometry, particularly on spaces with [[hyperbolic geometry]] or negative curvature. His joint work with [[Richard Canary]] and [[Yair Minsky]] resulted in a solution <ref>{{Cite journal|last=Brock|first=Jeffrey F.|last2=Canary|first2=Richard D.|last3=Minsky|first3=Yair N.|date=2012|title=The classification of Kleinian surface groups, II: The Ending Lamination Conjecture|jstor=23234164|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=176|issue=1|pages=1–149|doi=10.4007/annals.2012.176.1.1|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/0412006}}</ref> to the "Ending Lamination Conjecture" of [[William Thurston]], culminating in the geometric [[classification theorem]] for (topologically finite) hyperbolic 3-manifolds in terms of their fundamental group and the structure of their ends.

More recently, he has worked to understand applications of [[geometry]] and [[topology]] to the structure of massive and complex data sets and the risks and implications of the increasing use of 'black box' algorithms in science and society.

== Honors and awards ==
Source:<ref name=":0" />
* Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], 2017.
* Simons Fellowship (declined), 2016.
* [[John Simon Guggenheim Fellowship|John Simon Guggenheim]] Fellow, 2008.
* Donald D. Harrington Faculty Fellow, [[University of Texas at Austin]], 2003–2004.
* [[National Science Foundation]] Postdoctoral Fellow, [[Stanford University]], 1997–2000.
* [[Alfred P. Sloan]] Doctoral Dissertation Fellow, [[U.C. Berkeley]], 1996–1997.
* Outstanding Graduate Student Instructor Award, [[U.C. Berkeley]], 1996.
* [[National Science Foundation]] Graduate Fellow, [[U.C. Berkeley]], 1993–1996.
* Stanley and DeForest Mathematics Prizes, [[Yale University]], 1991 and 1992.

== Selected invited talks ==
Source:<ref name=":0" />
* Geometric Topology in Low Dimensions ([[University of Warwick]]), 2017.
* Geometry, Topology and Dynamics of Moduli Spaces ([[National University of Singapore]]), 2016.

== Selected publications ==
Source:<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/|title=MR: Search Publications database|website=mathscinet.ams.org|language=en|access-date=2018-03-19}}</ref>
* (with Nathan Dunfield) "Norms on the cohomology of hyperbolic 3-manifolds", ''Invent. Math.'' 210 (2017), no. 2, 531–558.
* (with [[Yair Minsky]], Hossein Namazi and Juan Souto), "Bounded combinatorics and uniform models for hyperbolic 3-manifolds." ''J. Topol.'' 9 (2016), no. 2, 451–501.
* (with [[Richard Canary]] and [[Yair Minsky]]) "The classification of Kleinian surface groups, II: The ending lamination conjecture." ''Ann. of Math. (2)'' 176 (2012), no. 1, 1–149.
* (with [[Benson Farb]]) "Curvature and rank of Teichmüller space." ''Amer. J. Math.'' 128 (2006), no. 1, 1–22.
* (with Kenneth Bromberg) "On the density of geometrically finite Kleinian groups." ''Acta Math.'' 192 (2004), no. 1, 33–93.
* "The Weil–Petersson metric and volumes of 3-dimensional hyperbolic convex cores." ''J. Amer. Math. Soc.'' 16 (2003), no. 3, 495–535.
* "Iteration of mapping classes and limits of hyperbolic 3-manifolds." ''Invent. Math.'' 143 (2001), no. 3, 523–570.
* "Boundaries of Teichmüller spaces and end-invariants for hyperbolic 3-manifolds." ''Duke Math. J.'' 106 (2001), no. 3, 527–552.
